analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/developer/build.md. The changed ranges (base 379-382, 390-391, 395-397, 569-571, 589-592, 596, 619-625; head 379-382, 390-391, 395-397, 569-571, 589-593, 595-596, 600, 623-628) describe CI runner routing and job-size behavior. The documented change is that the build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks jobs are now routed on the Darkbloom plane even while job sizes are off. Previously they kept their Blacksmith fallback and asked only when sizes were on. The patch excerpt was truncated, so the exact workflow edits that implement this are not visible.

No runtime provider code, protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The retained threat-model entries (T-041, TB-011, TB-002, TB-003) are not touched by the visible text.

The text at lines 396-400 and 573-575 notes that Darkbloom sandbox jobs use GitHub's Actions cache, not Blacksmith's. It also says route decisions fall back safely on error and that release, signing and publication keep literal Blacksmith labels (lines 561-562). I did not find a change that moves release or signing jobs onto the plane.

Open integration question: if the workflow changes behind this doc move build jobs, which produce the test-products artifacts, onto the Darkbloom plane, those jobs sit in a different trust and cache domain. Any test-product artifacts they upload, and the PR-scoped caches they restore, then derive from that plane. The doc keeps master caches strict, and release lanes are not routed. The actual workflow files were not supplied (provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml), so I cannot confirm that release lanes remain unrouted or that the route cannot influence signing. This is a documentation-only observation and not a finding.
